args.content:
# cli-args — exhaustive CLI surface map of /workspace/executable (tui-journal 0.16.1)

Method: ran the binary only, with fresh isolated HOME per experiment
(`env -i HOME=... XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.config XDG_DATA_HOME=$HOME/.local/share XDG_CACHE_HOME=$HOME/.cache XDG_STATE_HOME=$HOME/.local/state TERM=xterm-256color`),
plus a PTY harness for anything that initializes the TUI.
In the transcripts below `$HOME` stands for the per-run home dir; the binary interpolates
the real path into help text and `print-config` output at runtime.

## 0. Global conventions

- Exit codes: `0` success; `2` all clap/argument errors; `1` runtime errors (`Error: ...` on stderr).
- Help (`-h`, `--help`, `help`), `--version`, `print-config`, `theme print-path` output → **stdout**, exit 0.
- All clap errors and all runtime `Error:`/`INFO:` lines → **stderr**.
- No ANSI color/style sequences are emitted for help or errors, even when attached to a TTY (verified via PTY; only `\n` → `\r\n` pty translation happens).
- `-h` and `--help` produce byte-identical output (verified for top level and `import-journals`).
- Usage strings use the **basename of argv[0]** — via a symlink named `myjournal`, errors print `Usage: myjournal [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]`.
- `--version` / `-V` before any subcommand short-circuits: `executable --version print-config` → prints version, exit 0. `executable print-config --version` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '--version' found`.
- Every run (even plain `print-config` with no `-v`) creates the log file (see §8).

## 1. Top-level help (byte-exact, stdout, exit 0; `-h` == `--help`)

```
Tui app allows writing and managing journals/notes from within the terminal With different local back-ends

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  print-config     Print the current settings including the paths for the back-end files [aliases: pc]
  import-journals  Import journals from the given transfer JSON file to the current back-end file [aliases: imj]
  assign-priority  Assign priority for all the entries with empty priority field [aliases: ap]
  theme            Provides commands regarding changing themes and styles of the app [aliases: style]
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -j, --json-file-path <FILE PATH>    Sets the entries Json file path and starts using it
  -s, --sqlite-file-path <FILE PATH>  Sets the entries sqlite file path and starts using it
  -b, --backend-type <BACKEND_TYPE>   Sets the backend type and starts using it [possible values: json, sqlite]
  -c, --config <DIR PATH>             Specifies the path for the configuration directory.
                                      Configuration files is considered as root for themes file too.
                                      It still accepts the path for configuration file for backward compatibility.
                                      (default path: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tui-journal)
  -v, --verbose...                    Increases logging verbosity each use for up to 3 times
  -l, --log <FILE PATH>               Specifies a file to use for logging
                                      (default file: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui-journal/tui-journal.log)
  -h, --help                          Print help
  -V, --version                       Print version
```
- `(default path: ...)` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tui-journal` or `$HOME/.config/tui-journal` if XDG unset.
- `(default file: ...)` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui-journal/tui-journal.log` or `$HOME/.cache/tui-journal/tui-journal.log`.
- Both interpolated at runtime (help text changes with env).

`--version` / `-V` (stdout, exit 0, 19 bytes):
```
tui-journal 0.16.1
```

## 2. Subcommand help texts (all byte-exact, stdout, exit 0)

### `print-config --help` (alias `pc`) — 137 bytes
```
Print the current settings including the paths for the back-end files

Usage: executable print-config

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `import-journals --help` (alias `imj`) — 243 bytes
```
Import journals from the given transfer JSON file to the current back-end file

Usage: executable import-journals --path <FILE PATH>

Options:
  -p, --path <FILE PATH>  Path of the JSON file to import from
  -h, --help              Print help
```

### `assign-priority --help` (alias `ap`) — 202 bytes
```
Assign priority for all the entries with empty priority field

Usage: executable assign-priority <PRIORITY>

Arguments:
  <PRIORITY>  Priority value (Positive number)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `theme --help` (alias `style`) — 554 bytes
```
Provides commands regarding changing themes and styles of the app

Usage: executable theme <COMMAND>

Commands:
  print-path      Prints the path to the user themes file [aliases: path]
  print-default   Dumps the styles with the default values to be used as a reference and base for user custom themes [aliases: default]
  write-defaults  Creates user custom themes file if doesn't exist then writes the default styles to it [aliases: write]
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `theme print-path --help` (alias `path`) — 111 bytes
```
Prints the path to the user themes file

Usage: executable theme print-path

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `theme print-default --help` (alias `default`) — 173 bytes
```
Dumps the styles with the default values to be used as a reference and base for user custom themes

Usage: executable theme print-default

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `theme write-defaults --help` (alias `write`) — 161 bytes
```
Creates user custom themes file if doesn't exist then writes the default styles to it

Usage: executable theme write-defaults

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

Aliases produce the **identical** help text as the canonical name — the `Usage:` line always
shows the canonical names (`executable print-config`, `executable theme print-path`, etc.),
even when invoked as `pc --help`, `style path --help`, etc.

## 3. The `help` subcommand (all forms)

- `executable help` → byte-identical to top-level `--help` (stdout, exit 0).
- `executable help theme` == `executable theme help` == `theme --help` output (stdout, exit 0).
- `executable help theme print-path` == `executable theme help print-path` == `theme print-path --help`.
- Aliases resolve: `help pc`, `help style`, `help style path`, `help imj`, `help ap` all print the canonical command's help.
- `executable help help` (156 bytes, stdout, exit 0):
```
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: executable help [COMMAND]...

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]...  Print help for the subcommand(s)
```
- `help` takes ONLY subcommand names, no flags:
  - `executable help --help` → exit 2: `error: unrecognized subcommand '--help'` + top-level usage trailer.
  - `executable help -h` → exit 2: `error: unrecognized subcommand '-h'` + top-level usage trailer.
- Unknown path: `executable help nosuchcmd` → exit 2 `error: unrecognized subcommand 'nosuchcmd'` + top-level usage; `executable theme help nosuch` → exit 2 same message with `Usage: executable theme <COMMAND>`.
- Extra after leaf: `executable help print-config extra` → exit 2 `error: unrecognized subcommand 'extra'` with `Usage: executable print-config`.
- `executable theme print-path help` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument 'help' found` with `Usage: executable theme print-path` (leaf subcommands have no `help` child).

## 4. Unknown flags / subcommands (all stderr, exit 2)

Every clap error ends with the trailer (blank line before and after Usage):
```
\nUsage: <usage line>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n
```
(`--version`/help errors from value parsers omit the Usage part — see §6/§7.)

- `executable --nope` →
  ```
  error: unexpected argument '--nope' found

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- `executable -x` → same shape with `'-x'`.
- Near-miss long flag gets a tip; note the Usage line narrows to the suggested flag:
  ```
  $ executable --json
  error: unexpected argument '--json' found

    tip: a similar argument exists: '--json-file-path'

  Usage: executable --json-file-path <FILE PATH>

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- `executable import-journals --pat x` → tip `a similar argument exists: '--path'`, usage `Usage: executable import-journals --path <FILE PATH>`.
- `executable nosuchcmd` →
  ```
  error: unrecognized subcommand 'nosuchcmd'

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- `executable them` → adds `  tip: a similar subcommand exists: 'theme'`.
- `executable printconfig` → `  tip: some similar subcommands exist: 'pc', 'print-config'` (alias listed first!).
- `executable theme printpath` → `  tip: some similar subcommands exist: 'print-default', 'print-path'` with theme usage.
- `executable theme nosuch` / `executable theme --nope` → no tip, `Usage: executable theme <COMMAND>`.
- Bare positional: `executable 5` → `error: unrecognized subcommand '5'`.
- `executable theme print-path extra` → `error: unexpected argument 'extra' found`, `Usage: executable theme print-path`.

## 5. Missing values / duplicate flags (stderr, exit 2)

Missing value (no Usage block in these errors):
- `-j` / `--json-file-path` / `--json-file-path=` (empty `=` counts as missing!):
  `error: a value is required for '--json-file-path <FILE PATH>' but none was supplied`
- `-s`: `... '--sqlite-file-path <FILE PATH>' ...`
- `-b`:
  ```
  error: a value is required for '--backend-type <BACKEND_TYPE>' but none was supplied
    [possible values: json, sqlite]
  ```
- `-c`: `... '--config <DIR PATH>' ...`
- `-l`: `... '--log <FILE PATH>' ...`
- `import-journals -p` / `--path=` : `error: a value is required for '--path <FILE PATH>' but none was supplied`
All followed by `\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n` (no Usage line).

Duplicates (all exit 2, with full Usage trailer):
- `-j A -j B` → `error: the argument '--json-file-path <FILE PATH>' cannot be used multiple times`
- same shape for `-s`, `-b`, `-c`, `-l`, and `import-journals -p A -p B` (`'--path <FILE PATH>'`).

## 6. `-b/--backend-type` value validation (stderr, exit 2)

- Possible values are exactly lowercase `json`, `sqlite`; case-sensitive: `-b JSON`, `-b SQLite` rejected.
- `-b xml` →
  ```
  error: invalid value 'xml' for '--backend-type <BACKEND_TYPE>'
    [possible values: json, sqlite]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- Near-miss adds a tip line: `--backend-type jsonx` →
  ```
  error: invalid value 'jsonx' for '--backend-type <BACKEND_TYPE>'
    [possible values: json, sqlite]

    tip: a similar value exists: 'json'

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```

## 7. `-j` / `-s` / `-b` interactions (NO clap conflicts — all combos accepted)

Verified via `print-config` output (`backend_type` + the two `file_path` fields):

| args | resulting backend_type | json path | sqlite path |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | `Sqlite` | `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.json` | `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.db` |
| `-j /tmp/a.json` | **`Json`** | `/tmp/a.json` | default |
| `-s /tmp/b.db` | `Sqlite` | default | `/tmp/b.db` |
| `-b json` | `Json` | default | default |
| `-j X -s Y` (either order) | **`Sqlite`** | `X` | `Y` |
| `-j X -b json` | `Json` | `X` | default |
| `-j X -b sqlite` | `Sqlite` | `X` (unused) | default |
| `-s Y -b json` | `Json` | default | `Y` (unused) |
| `-j X -s Y -b json` | `Json` | `X` | `Y` |

Precedence rule: explicit `-b` always wins (any position); otherwise `-s` implies Sqlite and
beats `-j`'s implied Json; `-j` alone implies Json. Setting a path does NOT rewrite the other
backend's path. Both paths are always shown in `print-config` regardless of active backend.

Other syntax notes:
- `--json-file-path=/tmp/a.json` (equals form) works.
- Short-flag clustering works: `-vj /tmp/a.json` ≡ `-v -j /tmp/a.json`.
- `-v3` is parsed as `-v` + `-3` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '-3' found`.

## 8. `-v/--verbose` and `-l/--log`

- `-v` is a count flag, **not capped by clap**: `-vvvv` and `-v -v -v -v` are accepted, exit 0,
  no observable difference from `-vvv` ("up to 3 times" in help = effective cap at TRACE).
- Verbosity only affects the log file. Nothing else observable (stdout/stderr unchanged).
- Log file is ALWAYS created/truncated at startup, even with no `-v` and for non-TUI commands
  (`print-config` too): default `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui-journal/tui-journal.log`.
- Level mapping (observed via log contents after a brief TUI run, quit with `q`):
  - 0 (`-v` absent): file created, 0 bytes.
  - 1 (`-v`): file created, 0 bytes in a clean run (no records emitted).
  - 2 (`-vv`): DEBUG records appear (sqlx query logs), 15 DEBUG lines on fresh-db startup.
    First line e.g. `HH:MM:SS [DEBUG] (67) sqlx::query: summary="PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; …" ...`.
  - 3 (`-vvv`): TRACE. First line is always
    `HH:MM:SS [TRACE] (1) tjournal::logging: [src/logging.rs:38] Log initialized with level: TRACE`
    then `... [TRACE] (1) backend::sqlite: [/workspace/backend/src/sqlite/mod.rs:36] Creating Database with the URL 'sqlite://$HOME/tui-journal/entries.db'`, then the DEBUG sqlx lines.
  - 4+ (`-vvvv`): identical record set to `-vvv` (diffed; only timing/ordering noise).
  - Log line format: `HH:MM:SS [LEVEL] (thread_id) target: [src/file.rs:line] message`.
- `print-config -vvv` writes only the one TRACE "Log initialized" line (94 bytes).
- `-l <path>`: replaces the default log path entirely (default file NOT created).
  Parent directories are created recursively (tested 3 levels deep).
  The file is **truncated, not appended**, each launch (ran twice → single "Log initialized" line).
  With low verbosity the custom file is still created (0 bytes).
- `-l /tmp` (existing directory) → stderr, exit 1:
  `Error: Is a directory (os error 21)`
- XDG fallback: with all XDG vars unset, default log = `$HOME/.cache/tui-journal/tui-journal.log`.

## 9. `-c/--config` (dir vs file backward compatibility)

- Existing **directory** → config file read from `<dir>/config.toml`; themes root = `<dir>`
  (`-c <dir> theme print-path` → `<dir>/themes.toml`). Values in `config.toml` are applied
  (tested `backend_type = "Json"`, `scroll_per_page = 9`).
- Existing **file** (any name — tested `config.toml` and `weird.name`) → the file itself is the
  config (values applied). This is the documented backward-compat mode.
- Nonexistent path (whether it looks like a dir or file) → stderr, exit 1 (note the typo
  "exit" for "exist", byte-exact):
  `Error: Provided custom directory doesn't exit. Path: /tmp/tj/cli/no_such_dir`
- Malformed TOML (file contains `this is not toml!!!`) → stderr, exit 1, byte-exact with a
  trailing blank line (ends `=\`\n\n`):
  ```
  Error: Failed to read configuration file. Error infos: TOML parse error at line 1, column 6
    |
  1 | this is not toml!!!
    |      ^
  key with no value, expected `=`
  ```
- `-c <file>` + `theme print-path`: themes path is NOT derived from a file — stderr gets
  (note typo "themese", byte-exact)
  `INFO: Custom config directory is ignored in themese because it's not a directory.`
  and stdout still prints the **default** themes path (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tui-journal/themes.toml`),
  exit 0.
- Relative paths work (resolved against cwd). `~` is NOT expanded (`-c '~/foo'` → the
  "doesn't exit" error with literal `~/foo` in the message).
- Existing empty dir is fine (defaults used).
- `print-config` never creates the config dir; only the log file is created on disk.

## 10. Flags after subcommands / `--` handling

- Top-level options are NOT global — anywhere after the subcommand they error:
  - `print-config -j /tmp/a.json` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '-j' found`, `Usage: executable print-config`.
  - `print-config -v` → same with `'-v'`.
  - `theme print-path -j X` → same, `Usage: executable theme print-path`.
  - `assign-priority 5 -v` → exit 2:
    ```
    error: unexpected argument '-v' found

      tip: to pass '-v' as a value, use '-- -v'

    Usage: executable assign-priority <PRIORITY>
    ```
    (the tip appears because assign-priority has a positional).
- `--` before a subcommand blocks subcommand resolution:
  - `executable -- print-config` → exit 2:
    ```
    error: unexpected argument 'print-config' found

      tip: subcommand 'print-config' exists; to use it, remove the '--' before it

    Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]
    ```
  - `executable theme -- print-path` → same shape with `'print-path'` / theme usage.
  - `executable -- -j` → `error: unrecognized subcommand '-j'` + `  tip: a similar subcommand exists: 'import-journals'`.
- Trailing `--` is accepted: `print-config --` and `theme print-path --` both succeed normally.
- `--` before a positional passes it as a value: `assign-priority -- -5` reaches value parsing (§11).

## 11. `assign-priority <PRIORITY>`

- Type is **u32** (`0..=4294967295`). Despite the help saying "Positive number", `0` is accepted
  and works at runtime.
- Missing: exit 2:
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    <PRIORITY>

  Usage: executable assign-priority <PRIORITY>

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- Extra positional: `assign-priority 5 6` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '6' found` + ap usage.
- `assign-priority -5` (no `--`) → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '-5' found` + tip
  `to pass '-5' as a value, use '-- -5'`.
- `assign-priority -- -5` → exit 2 (no Usage block):
  `error: invalid value '-5' for '<PRIORITY>': -5 is not in 0..=4294967295`
- `assign-priority 4294967296` → `error: invalid value '4294967296' for '<PRIORITY>': 4294967296 is not in 0..=4294967295`
- `assign-priority 999999999999999999999999` (beyond u64) →
  `error: invalid value '999999999999999999999999' for '<PRIORITY>': number too large to fit in target type`
- `assign-priority abc` / `assign-priority 1.5` →
  `error: invalid value '<v>' for '<PRIORITY>': invalid digit found in string`
- `assign-priority +5` and `assign-priority 007` are ACCEPTED (Rust u32 parser: leading `+` and zeros OK).
- Runtime: requires a TTY. Without one, ANY valid value → stderr, exit 1:
  `Error: No such device or address (os error 6)`
- Under a TTY: enters alternate screen, shows a centered rounded-border popup
  `Assigning Priority to Journals...`, then drops into the normal full TUI (Journals/Content
  screen); `q` quits with exit 0. Side effects on first run: creates `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.db`
  (default Sqlite backend), `$HOME/.local/state/tui-journal/state.json`, and the log file.

## 12. `import-journals --path`

- `-p/--path <FILE PATH>` is required; missing → exit 2:
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    --path <FILE PATH>

  Usage: executable import-journals --path <FILE PATH>

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- Like assign-priority, the TUI initializes BEFORE any path validation: without a TTY every
  invocation (valid or not) fails with stderr `Error: No such device or address (os error 6)`, exit 1.
- Under a TTY: splash popup `Importing journals...` (rounded border), then the TUI opens;
  problems surface as a modal `Error` popup with an `(O)k` button, app stays in TUI:
  - nonexistent path → `Import file doesn't exist: path /tmp/tj/cli/nope.json`
  - path is a directory → `Error while parsing import file.` / `Error: Is a directory (os error 21)`
  - non-JSON content (`not json`) → `Error while parsing import file.` / `Error: expected ident at line 1 column 2`
  - `[]` → `Error while parsing import file.` / `Error: invalid length 0, expected struct EntriesDTO with 2 elements at line 1 column ...`
  - `{}` → `Error: missing field \`version\` at line 1 column 2`
  - `{"version":"0.16.1","entries":[]}` → `Error: invalid type: string "0.16.1", expected u16 at line 1 column 19`
- Valid minimal file: `{"version":1,"entries":[]}` (version is u16; 1, 3, 5 all accepted) →
  imports silently and shows the normal TUI, no success popup observed.

## 13. Path resolution summary (from help text + print-config + theme print-path)

- Config dir: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tui-journal` else `$HOME/.config/tui-journal`.
- Log file: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui-journal/tui-journal.log` else `$HOME/.cache/...`.
- App state dir: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tui-journal` else `$HOME/.local/state/tui-journal`.
- Themes file: `<config dir>/themes.toml`.
- Backend files: ALWAYS `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.json` and `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.db` —
  `XDG_DATA_HOME` is NOT used (verified with all XDG vars pointed elsewhere).
- Default `backend_type = "Sqlite"`.

## 14. Misc

- `executable theme` (no subcommand) → exit 2, and the full `theme --help` text is printed to
  **stderr** (byte-identical to the help output, 554 bytes).
- `executable` with no args launches the TUI (see tui-* notes).
- `--help`/`-h` anywhere valid short-circuits: `-j /a --help` prints top help, exit 0;
  `theme --help print-path` prints theme help, exit 0 (trailing args ignored).
- `executable print-config --` exit 0 (trailing `--` ok); `executable help` ignores nothing.

- No ANSI color/style sequences are emitted for help or errors, even when attached to a TTY (verified via PTY; only `\n` → `\r\n` pty translation happens).
- `-h` and `--help` produce byte-identical output (verified for top level and `import-journals`).
- Usage strings use the **basename of argv[0]** — via a symlink named `myjournal`, errors print `Usage: myjournal [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]`.
- `--version` / `-V` before any subcommand short-circuits: `executable --version print-config` → prints version, exit 0. `executable print-config --version` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '--version' found`.
- Every run (even plain `print-config` with no `-v`) creates the log file (see §8).

## 1. Top-level help (byte-exact, stdout, exit 0; `-h` == `--help`)

```
Tui app allows writing and managing journals/notes from within the terminal With different local back-ends

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  print-config     Print the current settings including the paths for the back-end files [aliases: pc]
  import-journals  Import journals from the given transfer JSON file to the current back-end file [aliases: imj]
  assign-priority  Assign priority for all the entries with empty priority field [aliases: ap]
  theme            Provides commands regarding changing themes and styles of the app [aliases: style]
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -j, --json-file-path <FILE PATH>    Sets the entries Json file path and starts using it
  -s, --sqlite-file-path <FILE PATH>  Sets the entries sqlite file path and starts using it
  -b, --backend-type <BACKEND_TYPE>   Sets the backend type and starts using it [possible values: json, sqlite]
  -c, --config <DIR PATH>             Specifies the path for the configuration directory.
                                      Configuration files is considered as root for themes file too.
                                      It still accepts the path for configuration file for backward compatibility.
                                      (default path: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tui-journal)
  -v, --verbose...                    Increases logging verbosity each use for up to 3 times
  -l, --log <FILE PATH>               Specifies a file to use for logging
                                      (default file: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui-journal/tui-journal.log)
  -h, --help                          Print help
  -V, --version                       Print version
```
- `(default path: ...)` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tui-journal` or `$HOME/.config/tui-journal` if XDG unset.
- `(default file: ...)` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui-journal/tui-journal.log` or `$HOME/.cache/tui-journal/tui-journal.log`.
- Both interpolated at runtime (help text changes with env).

`--version` / `-V` (stdout, exit 0, 19 bytes):
```
tui-journal 0.16.1
```

## 2. Subcommand help texts (all byte-exact, stdout, exit 0)

### `print-config --help` (alias `pc`) — 137 bytes
```
Print the current settings including the paths for the back-end files

Usage: executable print-config

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `import-journals --help` (alias `imj`) — 243 bytes
```
Import journals from the given transfer JSON file to the current back-end file

Usage: executable import-journals --path <FILE PATH>

Options:
  -p, --path <FILE PATH>  Path of the JSON file to import from
  -h, --help              Print help
```

### `assign-priority --help` (alias `ap`) — 202 bytes
```
Assign priority for all the entries with empty priority field

Usage: executable assign-priority <PRIORITY>

Arguments:
  <PRIORITY>  Priority value (Positive number)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `theme --help` (alias `style`) — 554 bytes
```
Provides commands regarding changing themes and styles of the app

Usage: executable theme <COMMAND>

Commands:
  print-path      Prints the path to the user themes file [aliases: path]
  print-default   Dumps the styles with the default values to be used as a reference and base for user custom themes [aliases: default]
  write-defaults  Creates user custom themes file if doesn't exist then writes the default styles to it [aliases: write]
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `theme print-path --help` (alias `path`) — 111 bytes
```
Prints the path to the user themes file

Usage: executable theme print-path

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `theme print-default --help` (alias `default`) — 173 bytes
```
Dumps the styles with the default values to be used as a reference and base for user custom themes

Usage: executable theme print-default

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

### `theme write-defaults --help` (alias `write`) — 161 bytes
```
Creates user custom themes file if doesn't exist then writes the default styles to it

Usage: executable theme write-defaults

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

Aliases produce the **identical** help text as the canonical name — the `Usage:` line always
shows the canonical names (`executable print-config`, `executable theme print-path`, etc.),
even when invoked as `pc --help`, `style path --help`, etc.

## 3. The `help` subcommand (all forms)

- `executable help` → byte-identical to top-level `--help` (stdout, exit 0).
- `executable help theme` == `executable theme help` == `theme --help` output (stdout, exit 0).
- `executable help theme print-path` == `executable theme help print-path` == `theme print-path --help`.
- Aliases resolve: `help pc`, `help style`, `help style path`, `help imj`, `help ap` all print the canonical command's help.
- `executable help help` (156 bytes, stdout, exit 0):
```
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: executable help [COMMAND]...

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]...  Print help for the subcommand(s)
```
- `help` takes ONLY subcommand names, no flags:
  - `executable help --help` → exit 2: `error: unrecognized subcommand '--help'` + top-level usage trailer.
  - `executable help -h` → exit 2: `error: unrecognized subcommand '-h'` + top-level usage trailer.
- Unknown path: `executable help nosuchcmd` → exit 2 `error: unrecognized subcommand 'nosuchcmd'` + top-level usage; `executable theme help nosuch` → exit 2 same message with `Usage: executable theme <COMMAND>`.
- Extra after leaf: `executable help print-config extra` → exit 2 `error: unrecognized subcommand 'extra'` with `Usage: executable print-config`.
- `executable theme print-path help` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument 'help' found` with `Usage: executable theme print-path` (leaf subcommands have no `help` child).

## 4. Unknown flags / subcommands (all stderr, exit 2)

Every clap error ends with the trailer (blank line before and after Usage):
```
\nUsage: <usage line>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n
```
(`--version`/help errors from value parsers omit the Usage part — see §6/§7.)

- `executable --nope` →
  ```
  error: unexpected argument '--nope' found

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- `executable -x` → same shape with `'-x'`.
- Near-miss long flag gets a tip; note the Usage line narrows to the suggested flag:
  ```
  $ executable --json
  error: unexpected argument '--json' found

    tip: a similar argument exists: '--json-file-path'

  Usage: executable --json-file-path <FILE PATH>

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- `executable import-journals --pat x` → tip `a similar argument exists: '--path'`, usage `Usage: executable import-journals --path <FILE PATH>`.
- `executable nosuchcmd` →
  ```
  error: unrecognized subcommand 'nosuchcmd'

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- `executable them` → adds `  tip: a similar subcommand exists: 'theme'`.
- `executable printconfig` → `  tip: some similar subcommands exist: 'pc', 'print-config'` (alias listed first!).
- `executable theme printpath` → `  tip: some similar subcommands exist: 'print-default', 'print-path'` with theme usage.
- `executable theme nosuch` / `executable theme --nope` → no tip, `Usage: executable theme <COMMAND>`.
- Bare positional: `executable 5` → `error: unrecognized subcommand '5'`.
- `executable theme print-path extra` → `error: unexpected argument 'extra' found`, `Usage: executable theme print-path`.

## 5. Missing values / duplicate flags (stderr, exit 2)

Missing value (no Usage block in these errors):
- `-j` / `--json-file-path` / `--json-file-path=` (empty `=` counts as missing!):
  `error: a value is required for '--json-file-path <FILE PATH>' but none was supplied`
- `-s`: `... '--sqlite-file-path <FILE PATH>' ...`
- `-b`:
  ```
  error: a value is required for '--backend-type <BACKEND_TYPE>' but none was supplied
    [possible values: json, sqlite]
  ```
- `-c`: `... '--config <DIR PATH>' ...`
- `-l`: `... '--log <FILE PATH>' ...`
- `import-journals -p` / `--path=` : `error: a value is required for '--path <FILE PATH>' but none was supplied`
All followed by `\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n` (no Usage line).

Duplicates (all exit 2, with full Usage trailer):
- `-j A -j B` → `error: the argument '--json-file-path <FILE PATH>' cannot be used multiple times`
- same shape for `-s`, `-b`, `-c`, `-l`, and `import-journals -p A -p B` (`'--path <FILE PATH>'`).

## 6. `-b/--backend-type` value validation (stderr, exit 2)

- Possible values are exactly lowercase `json`, `sqlite`; case-sensitive: `-b JSON`, `-b SQLite` rejected.
- `-b xml` →
  ```
  error: invalid value 'xml' for '--backend-type <BACKEND_TYPE>'
    [possible values: json, sqlite]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- Near-miss adds a tip line: `--backend-type jsonx` →
  ```
  error: invalid value 'jsonx' for '--backend-type <BACKEND_TYPE>'
    [possible values: json, sqlite]

    tip: a similar value exists: 'json'

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```

## 7. `-j` / `-s` / `-b` interactions (NO clap conflicts — all combos accepted)

Verified via `print-config` output (`backend_type` + the two `file_path` fields):

| args | resulting backend_type | json path | sqlite path |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | `Sqlite` | `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.json` | `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.db` |
| `-j /tmp/a.json` | **`Json`** | `/tmp/a.json` | default |
| `-s /tmp/b.db` | `Sqlite` | default | `/tmp/b.db` |
| `-b json` | `Json` | default | default |
| `-j X -s Y` (either order) | **`Sqlite`** | `X` | `Y` |
| `-j X -b json` | `Json` | `X` | default |
| `-j X -b sqlite` | `Sqlite` | `X` (unused) | default |
| `-s Y -b json` | `Json` | default | `Y` (unused) |
| `-j X -s Y -b json` | `Json` | `X` | `Y` |

Precedence rule: explicit `-b` always wins (any position); otherwise `-s` implies Sqlite and
beats `-j`'s implied Json; `-j` alone implies Json. Setting a path does NOT rewrite the other
backend's path. Both paths are always shown in `print-config` regardless of active backend.

Other syntax notes:
- `--json-file-path=/tmp/a.json` (equals form) works.
- Short-flag clustering works: `-vj /tmp/a.json` ≡ `-v -j /tmp/a.json`.
- `-v3` is parsed as `-v` + `-3` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '-3' found`.

## 8. `-v/--verbose` and `-l/--log`

- `-v` is a count flag, **not capped by clap**: `-vvvv` and `-v -v -v -v` are accepted, exit 0,
  no observable difference from `-vvv` ("up to 3 times" in help = effective cap at TRACE).
- Verbosity only affects the log file. Nothing else observable (stdout/stderr unchanged).
- Log file is ALWAYS created/truncated at startup, even with no `-v` and for non-TUI commands
  (`print-config` too): default `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui-journal/tui-journal.log`.
- Level mapping (observed via log contents after a brief TUI run, quit with `q`):
  - 0 (`-v` absent): file created, 0 bytes.
  - 1 (`-v`): file created, 0 bytes in a clean run (no records emitted).
  - 2 (`-vv`): DEBUG records appear (sqlx query logs), 15 DEBUG lines on fresh-db startup.
    First line e.g. `HH:MM:SS [DEBUG] (67) sqlx::query: summary="PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; …" ...`.
  - 3 (`-vvv`): TRACE. First line is always
    `HH:MM:SS [TRACE] (1) tjournal::logging: [src/logging.rs:38] Log initialized with level: TRACE`
    then `... [TRACE] (1) backend::sqlite: [/workspace/backend/src/sqlite/mod.rs:36] Creating Database with the URL 'sqlite://$HOME/tui-journal/entries.db'`, then the DEBUG sqlx lines.
  - 4+ (`-vvvv`): identical record set to `-vvv` (diffed; only timing/ordering noise).
  - Log line format: `HH:MM:SS [LEVEL] (thread_id) target: [src/file.rs:line] message`.
- `print-config -vvv` writes only the one TRACE "Log initialized" line (94 bytes).
- `-l <path>`: replaces the default log path entirely (default file NOT created).
  Parent directories are created recursively (tested 3 levels deep).
  The file is **truncated, not appended**, each launch (ran twice → single "Log initialized" line).
  With low verbosity the custom file is still created (0 bytes).
- `-l /tmp` (existing directory) → stderr, exit 1:
  `Error: Is a directory (os error 21)`
- XDG fallback: with all XDG vars unset, default log = `$HOME/.cache/tui-journal/tui-journal.log`.

## 9. `-c/--config` (dir vs file backward compatibility)

- Existing **directory** → config file read from `<dir>/config.toml`; themes root = `<dir>`
  (`-c <dir> theme print-path` → `<dir>/themes.toml`). Values in `config.toml` are applied
  (tested `backend_type = "Json"`, `scroll_per_page = 9`).
- Existing **file** (any name — tested `config.toml` and `weird.name`) → the file itself is the
  config (values applied). This is the documented backward-compat mode.
- Nonexistent path (whether it looks like a dir or file) → stderr, exit 1 (note the typo
  "exit" for "exist", byte-exact):
  `Error: Provided custom directory doesn't exit. Path: /tmp/tj/cli/no_such_dir`
- Malformed TOML (file contains `this is not toml!!!`) → stderr, exit 1, byte-exact with a
  trailing blank line (ends `=\`\n\n`):
  ```
  Error: Failed to read configuration file. Error infos: TOML parse error at line 1, column 6
    |
  1 | this is not toml!!!
    |      ^
  key with no value, expected `=`
  ```
- `-c <file>` + `theme print-path`: themes path is NOT derived from a file — stderr gets
  (note typo "themese", byte-exact)
  `INFO: Custom config directory is ignored in themese because it's not a directory.`
  and stdout still prints the **default** themes path (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tui-journal/themes.toml`),
  exit 0.
- Relative paths work (resolved against cwd). `~` is NOT expanded (`-c '~/foo'` → the
  "doesn't exit" error with literal `~/foo` in the message).
- Existing empty dir is fine (defaults used).
- `print-config` never creates the config dir; only the log file is created on disk.

## 10. Flags after subcommands / `--` handling

- Top-level options are NOT global — anywhere after the subcommand they error:
  - `print-config -j /tmp/a.json` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '-j' found`, `Usage: executable print-config`.
  - `print-config -v` → same with `'-v'`.
  - `theme print-path -j X` → same, `Usage: executable theme print-path`.
  - `assign-priority 5 -v` → exit 2:
    ```
    error: unexpected argument '-v' found

      tip: to pass '-v' as a value, use '-- -v'

    Usage: executable assign-priority <PRIORITY>
    ```
    (the tip appears because assign-priority has a positional).
- `--` before a subcommand blocks subcommand resolution:
  - `executable -- print-config` → exit 2:
    ```
    error: unexpected argument 'print-config' found

      tip: subcommand 'print-config' exists; to use it, remove the '--' before it

    Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]
    ```
  - `executable theme -- print-path` → same shape with `'print-path'` / theme usage.
  - `executable -- -j` → `error: unrecognized subcommand '-j'` + `  tip: a similar subcommand exists: 'import-journals'`.
- Trailing `--` is accepted: `print-config --` and `theme print-path --` both succeed normally.
- `--` before a positional passes it as a value: `assign-priority -- -5` reaches value parsing (§11).

## 11. `assign-priority <PRIORITY>`

- Type is **u32** (`0..=4294967295`). Despite the help saying "Positive number", `0` is accepted
  and works at runtime.
- Missing: exit 2:
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    <PRIORITY>

  Usage: executable assign-priority <PRIORITY>

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- Extra positional: `assign-priority 5 6` → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '6' found` + ap usage.
- `assign-priority -5` (no `--`) → exit 2 `error: unexpected argument '-5' found` + tip
  `to pass '-5' as a value, use '-- -5'`.
- `assign-priority -- -5` → exit 2 (no Usage block):
  `error: invalid value '-5' for '<PRIORITY>': -5 is not in 0..=4294967295`
- `assign-priority 4294967296` → `error: invalid value '4294967296' for '<PRIORITY>': 4294967296 is not in 0..=4294967295`
- `assign-priority 999999999999999999999999` (beyond u64) →
  `error: invalid value '999999999999999999999999' for '<PRIORITY>': number too large to fit in target type`
- `assign-priority abc` / `assign-priority 1.5` →
  `error: invalid value '<v>' for '<PRIORITY>': invalid digit found in string`
- `assign-priority +5` and `assign-priority 007` are ACCEPTED (Rust u32 parser: leading `+` and zeros OK).
- Runtime: requires a TTY. Without one, ANY valid value → stderr, exit 1:
  `Error: No such device or address (os error 6)`
- Under a TTY: enters alternate screen, shows a centered rounded-border popup
  `Assigning Priority to Journals...`, then drops into the normal full TUI (Journals/Content
  screen); `q` quits with exit 0. Side effects on first run: creates `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.db`
  (default Sqlite backend), `$HOME/.local/state/tui-journal/state.json`, and the log file.

## 12. `import-journals --path`

- `-p/--path <FILE PATH>` is required; missing → exit 2:
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    --path <FILE PATH>

  Usage: executable import-journals --path <FILE PATH>

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- Like assign-priority, the TUI initializes BEFORE any path validation: without a TTY every
  invocation (valid or not) fails with stderr `Error: No such device or address (os error 6)`, exit 1.
- Under a TTY: splash popup `Importing journals...` (rounded border), then the TUI opens;
  problems surface as a modal `Error` popup with an `(O)k` button, app stays in TUI:
  - nonexistent path → `Import file doesn't exist: path /tmp/tj/cli/nope.json`
  - path is a directory → `Error while parsing import file.` / `Error: Is a directory (os error 21)`
  - non-JSON content (`not json`) → `Error while parsing import file.` / `Error: expected ident at line 1 column 2`
  - `[]` → `Error while parsing import file.` / `Error: invalid length 0, expected struct EntriesDTO with 2 elements at line 1 column ...`
  - `{}` → `Error: missing field \`version\` at line 1 column 2`
  - `{"version":"0.16.1","entries":[]}` → `Error: invalid type: string "0.16.1", expected u16 at line 1 column 19`
- Valid minimal file: `{"version":1,"entries":[]}` (version is u16; 1, 3, 5 all accepted) →
  imports silently and shows the normal TUI, no success popup observed.

## 13. Path resolution summary (from help text + print-config + theme print-path)

- Config dir: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tui-journal` else `$HOME/.config/tui-journal`.
- Log file: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui-journal/tui-journal.log` else `$HOME/.cache/...`.
- App state dir: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tui-journal` else `$HOME/.local/state/tui-journal`.
- Themes file: `<config dir>/themes.toml`.
- Backend files: ALWAYS `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.json` and `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.db` —
  `XDG_DATA_HOME` is NOT used (verified with all XDG vars pointed elsewhere).
- Default `backend_type = "Sqlite"`.

## 14. Misc

- `executable theme` (no subcommand) → exit 2, and the full `theme --help` text is printed to
  **stderr** (byte-identical to the help output, 554 bytes).
- `executable` with no args launches the TUI (see tui-* notes).
- `--help`/`-h` anywhere valid short-circuits: `-j /a --help` prints top help, exit 0;
  `theme --help print-path` prints theme help, exit 0 (trailing args ignored).
- `executable print-config --` exit 0 (trailing `--` ok); `executable help` ignores nothing.

payload.resultSummary:
Done. Full notes written to `/tmp/tj/notes/cli-args.md` (~21 KB, all outputs byte-exact with exit codes and streams). Key findings:

**Help surface**
- Top help, `print-config`/`import-journals`/`assign-priority`/`theme` + all 3 theme subcommands captured byte-exact; `-h` == `--help` always; aliases (`pc/imj/ap/style/path/default/write`) print canonical names in `Usage:` lines. Help text interpolates `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` defaults at runtime.
- `help` subcommand: `help`, `help theme`, `theme help`, `help theme print-path`, `theme help print-path`, `help help` all mapped; `help` accepts only subcommand names (`help -h`/`help --help` → "unrecognized subcommand" errors, exit 2).

**Error grammar (clap v4)**
- Exit 2 for all arg errors (stderr), exit 1 for runtime `Error: ...` (stderr), stdout only for help/version/print-config/print-path. No ANSI colors even on TTY. Usage strings use argv[0] basename.
- Unknown flags/subcommands with near-miss tips (incl. alias-first tip `'pc', 'print-config'`); missing-value errors omit the Usage block; `--flag=` (empty) counts as missing; every value flag errors "cannot be used multiple times" if repeated.

**Flag semantics**
- No clap conflicts: `-j` implies Json backend, `-s` implies Sqlite and **wins over `-j` regardless of order**, explicit `-b` overrides both. Full precedence table in notes.
- `-b` values lowercase-only `json`/`sqlite`; `assign-priority` takes u32 (`0` accepted despite "Positive number"; `+5`, `007` ok; `-5` via `--` gives range error; exact texts for huge/non-numeric recorded).
- Top-level flags after subcommands → "unexpected argument" errors; `--` before a subcommand gives the "remove the '--'" tip; trailing `--` is fine.

**Logging**
- Log file always created/truncated (even `print-config`, no `-v`). Levels: 0–1 → empty in clean runs, 2 → DEBUG (sqlx), 3 → TRACE (first line `Log initialized with level: TRACE`); `-vvvv` ≡ `-vvv`, no cap error. `-l` replaces default path, creates parent dirs recursively, truncates each run, `-l <dir>` → `Error: Is a directory (os error 21)`.

**`-c` backward compat**
- Existing dir → `<dir>/config.toml`; existing file (any name) → used directly; nonexistent → `Error: Provided custom directory doesn't exit. Path: ...` (typo "exit" verbatim); malformed TOML → full `TOML parse error` block with trailing blank line; `-c <file>` + `theme print-path` → stderr `INFO: Custom config directory is ignored in themese because it's not a directory.` (typo "themese" verbatim) while stdout prints the default themes path, exit 0. `~` not expanded; relative paths work.

**TTY-gated subcommands**
- `assign-priority`/`import-journals` initialize the TUI before any validation — without a TTY everything fails `Error: No such device or address (os error 6)`. Under PTY: splash popups (`Assigning Priority to Journals...`, `Importing journals...`), then the full TUI. Import validation errors appear as modal popups (exact texts for nonexistent/dir/bad-JSON/`[]`/`{}`/string-version recorded); minimal valid file is `{"version":1,"entries":[]}` (version is u16).

Scratch files live under `/tmp/tj/cli/` (run.sh helper, ptyrun.py, per-experiment homes) if anyone needs to reproduce.

 'date_offset': '{"version":100,"entries":[{"date":"2021-01-01T10:20:30+03:00","title":"T","content":"c","tags":[],"priority":1}]}',

}
for name, content in variants.items():

# Scope: theme-cmd — theme subcommands & themes.toml handling

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (`tui-journal 0.16.1`). All findings from black-box runs only.
All runs used fresh isolated HOME dirs under `/tmp/tj/theme/*` (`env -i HOME=... PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`).
Harness quirk (affects all PTY experiments): the FIRST keypress sent after TUI startup is
swallowed (app enables raw mode after first draw). Send a dummy key first, or send real keys twice.

---

## 1. `theme` subcommand surface

`./executable theme --help` (exit 0, stdout, LF endings):

```
Provides commands regarding changing themes and styles of the app

Usage: executable theme <COMMAND>

Commands:
  print-path      Prints the path to the user themes file [aliases: path]
  print-default   Dumps the styles with the default values to be used as a reference and base for user custom themes [aliases: default]
  write-defaults  Creates user custom themes file if doesn't exist then writes the default styles to it [aliases: write]
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

- `theme` is also aliased as `style` (top level). Sub-aliases verified working:
  `theme path`, `theme default`, `theme write`, `style path`, `theme help`.
- Bare `./executable theme` → prints the same help text to **stderr**, exit **2** (554 bytes on stderr, 0 on stdout).
- `./executable theme bogus` → stderr, exit **2**:
  ```
  error: unrecognized subcommand 'bogus'

  Usage: executable theme <COMMAND>

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- `theme print-path --help` → `Prints the path to the user themes file\n\nUsage: executable theme print-path\n\nOptions:\n  -h, --help  Print help\n` (exit 0).
- `theme print-default --help` → `Dumps the styles with the default values to be used as a reference and base for user custom themes\n\nUsage: executable theme print-default\n\nOptions:\n  -h, --help  Print help\n` (exit 0).
- `theme write-defaults --help` → same shape with its one-line description (exit 0).
- Every invocation (even `theme print-path`) creates `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui-journal/tui-journal.log`
  (or `$HOME/.cache/tui-journal/tui-journal.log`) as a side effect.

## 2. `theme print-default` — byte-exact output

Command: `./executable theme print-default`. Exit 0, stderr empty, stdout = **1794 bytes, 116 lines**
(LF endings, no ANSI escapes, no trailing spaces). The text is the default themes TOML followed by an
extra blank line (i.e. the TOML string ends with `\n` and is printed with an additional `\n`).
Byte-exact content (`$` marks line ends, no trailing whitespace anywhere):

```
[general.input_block_active]$
fg = "LightYellow"$
modifiers = ""$
$
[general.input_block_invalid]$
fg = "LightRed"$
modifiers = ""$

[general.input_corsur_active]$
fg = "Black"$
bg = "LightYellow"$

(Exact copy also at `/tmp/tj/theme/print-default.out`.)

Note: the default dump contains NO `underline_color` lines and NO `bg` on styles that don't need one —
only fields differing from type-defaults are serialized. `msgbox` values are bare color strings, not style tables.

## 3. `theme print-path` — path resolution

Output is the path + `\n` on stdout, exit 0. It does NOT create any directory.
Resolution rules (verified):

| Environment / flags | Output |
|---|---|
| `HOME=/h` only | `/h/.config/tui-journal/themes.toml` |
| `HOME=/h XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/x` | `/x/tui-journal/themes.toml` |
| `HOME=/h XDG_CONFIG_HOME=` (empty) | `/h/.config/tui-journal/themes.toml` (empty XDG ignored) |
| no HOME, no XDG (env -i) | `/root/.config/tui-journal/themes.toml` (falls back to passwd entry) |
| `-c /existing/dir` | `/existing/dir/themes.toml` |
| `-c existing/dir` (relative, cwd=/tmp/tj/theme) | `existing/dir/themes.toml` (printed relative, exactly as joined) |
| `-c /nonexistent` | stderr: `Error: Provided custom directory doesn't exit. Path: /nonexistent` — exit **1** (note typo "exit") |
| `-c /path/to/file.toml` (existing FILE, not dir) | stderr: `INFO: Custom config directory is ignored in themese because it's not a directory.` then stdout prints the DEFAULT path (`$HOME/.config/tui-journal/themes.toml`), exit **0** (note typo "themese") |
| `-c ~/cfg` | tilde NOT expanded → `Error: Provided custom directory doesn't exit. Path: ~/cfg`, exit 1 |
| `-c /dir/` (trailing slash) | `/dir/themes.toml` (slash normalized) |

The themes file name is **`themes.toml`** (plural). Bundled `/workspace/THEMES.md` says `theme.toml`
(singular) — that is WRONG for this binary; a file named `theme.toml` is completely ignored (TUI starts with defaults).

## 4. `theme write-defaults`

- Config dir does not exist → **fails**, exit 1, stdout empty, stderr exactly:
  ```
  Error: Error while writing default themes to file

  Caused by:
      No such file or directory (os error 2)
  ```
  It NEVER creates directories (fails the same way whether the missing part is
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` itself or the `tui-journal` subdir or `$HOME/.config/tui-journal`).
- Config dir exists, no themes.toml → creates `<dir>/themes.toml`, stdout:
  `Default themes have been written to <abs path>/themes.toml\n`, exit 0, stderr empty.
  Written file is **1793 bytes, mode 0644**, byte-identical to `print-default` output MINUS the final
  newline (file ends `...question = "LightBlue"\n`; print-default adds one more `\n`).
- themes.toml already exists (even 0-byte file, even a DIRECTORY named themes.toml) → exit 1, stderr:
  `Error: Themes file already exists. Path: <path>` — pure existence check, no content comparison, file untouched.
- Honors `-c <dir>` the same way as print-path.
- Not affected by a malformed existing themes.toml (it never reads the file).

## 5. How the TUI consumes themes.toml

### 5.1 Loading & error behavior

- Themes are loaded at startup BEFORE the terminal is initialized (before alternate screen). A bad
  themes.toml makes the app exit **1** without touching the screen; the whole error goes to **stderr**
  (LF endings on a pipe; `\r\n` under the PTY). Nothing on stdout.
- Error shape (anyhow-style chain), e.g. for `fg = "NotAColor"` under `[journals_list.block_active]`:
  ```
  Error: Error while retrieving app styles

  Caused by:

All runs used fresh isolated HOME dirs under `/tmp/tj/theme/*` (`env -i HOME=... PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`).
Harness quirk (affects all PTY experiments): the FIRST keypress sent after TUI startup is
swallowed (app enables raw mode after first draw). Send a dummy key first, or send real keys twice.

---

## 1. `theme` subcommand surface

`./executable theme --help` (exit 0, stdout, LF endings):

```
Provides commands regarding changing themes and styles of the app

Usage: executable theme <COMMAND>

Commands:
  print-path      Prints the path to the user themes file [aliases: path]
  print-default   Dumps the styles with the default values to be used as a reference and base for user custom themes [aliases: default]
  write-defaults  Creates user custom themes file if doesn't exist then writes the default styles to it [aliases: write]
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

- `theme` is also aliased as `style` (top level). Sub-aliases verified working:
  `theme path`, `theme default`, `theme write`, `style path`, `theme help`.
- Bare `./executable theme` → prints the same help text to **stderr**, exit **2** (554 bytes on stderr, 0 on stdout).

payload.resultSummary:
Done. Full notes are in `/tmp/tj/notes/theme-cmd.md`; key findings:

**CLI surface**
- `theme` (alias `style`) with `print-path`/`path`, `print-default`/`default`, `write-defaults`/`write`. Bare `theme` → help on stderr, exit 2. Unknown subcommand → clap error, exit 2.
- `print-default`: exit 0, exactly **1794 bytes / 116 lines** (byte-exact copy in the notes and at `/tmp/tj/theme/print-default.out`); ends with an extra blank line.

**print-path resolution**
- `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tui-journal/themes.toml` else `$HOME/.config/tui-journal/themes.toml` (empty XDG ignored; no HOME → passwd fallback `/root`). Filename is **`themes.toml`** — THEMES.md's `theme.toml` is wrong and ignored.
- `-c` must be an **existing directory** (relative ok, tilde not expanded): nonexistent → `Error: Provided custom directory doesn't exit. Path: ...`, exit 1 (typo "exit" verbatim). An existing *file* → stderr `INFO: Custom config directory is ignored in themese because it's not a directory.` (typo "themese") and falls back to the default path, exit 0.

**write-defaults**
- Never creates directories: missing config dir → `Error: Error while writing default themes to file\n\nCaused by:\n    No such file or directory (os error 2)`, exit 1.
- Success → `Default themes have been written to <path>` on stdout; file is **1793 bytes** = print-default output minus the final newline.
- Run twice / existing file (even empty, even a directory named themes.toml) → `Error: Themes file already exists. Path: ...`, exit 1; pure existence check.

**TUI consumption of themes.toml**
- Loaded before terminal init; any parse failure → exit 1, nothing on screen, anyhow chain on stderr: `Error: Error while retrieving app styles` → `0: Error while desrializing toml text to styles. File path: ...` (typo "desrializing") → `1: TOML parse error ...` with parser excerpt/caret. Inner messages: `Failed to parse Colors`, `... untagged enum ColorFormat`, `unrecognized named flag \`X\``, `invalid type: ... expected struct GeneralStyles|JournalsListStyles|EditorStyles|MsgBoxColors|Style`.
- Unknown keys/tables silently ignored everywhere; empty file fine; bad file doesn't affect other subcommands.
- Color names case-insensitive (16 basic names, Grey/Gray both ok); hex exactly `#RRGGBB`; modifiers case-SENSITIVE, `|`-separated, whitespace tolerated.
- **Override semantics:** a style table in themes.toml rebuilds the whole style from type defaults — setting only `fg` wipes the shipped default `BOLD`.
- **Rendering:** this build emits **no fg/bg color SGR sequences at all** (any TERM, any theme, default highlight/msgbox included) — only modifier SGRs (`1/22, 2/22, 3/23, 4/24, 7/27, 9/29`) plus `ESC[;m`/`ESC[m`/`ESC[0m` markers. Changed fg colors change nothing in the byte stream; changed modifiers do.
- Harness quirk: the first keypress after TUI startup is swallowed — send a dummy key first.

from exp import exp
from vtparse_ed import Screen

def probe(name, keys, wait=0.8):
    out = exp(name, keys=b'\r', post_wait=0.5, stdin_after=[(b'\x1b',0.3),(keys,wait)])
    s = Screen(24,80); s.feed(out)
    lines = s.render().splitlines()
    content = [l[25:79].rstrip() for l in lines[1:5]]
    print(name, '->', content)

# cursor starts at line3 past-end. kk moves to line1 col6 ('X')

    ('kk0x', b'kk0x'),      # 0 = line start? then x deletes 'H'
    ('kk_dollar_x', b'kk$x'),# $ = line end? x deletes 'e'
    ('kkGx', b'kkGx'),      # G = last line?
    ('kkex', b'kkex'),      # e = word end? X is in 'HelloXYZabcde' one word
    ('kkjx', b'kkjx'),      # j down to line2 col6(past-end) x deletes newline?
    ('kklx', b'kklx'),      # l right to 'Y', x deletes 'Y'
    ('kkdd', b'kkdd'),      # dd deletes line1?
    ('kkdw', b'kkdw'),      # dw deletes word?
    ('kkD', b'kkD'),        # D delete to EOL?
    ('kkcc', b'kkcc'),      # cc change line?
]:
    probe(name, keys)
EOF

args.content:
# backends-data — data/back-end formats of tui-journal 0.16.1

All experiments with fresh isolated HOMEs under `/tmp/tj/bd/homeN`, XDG_* pointed inside
the same HOME. TUI driven via `/tmp/tj/harness.py` and `/tmp/tj/bd/runpty.py` (pty + exit code).

## 1. JSON backend (`-b json`): `$HOME/tui-journal/entries.json`

### Exact file format
- **Single line, compact JSON array, NO spaces, NO trailing newline.** Example (3 entries, byte-exact):
```
[{"id":0,"date":"2026-08-09T00:00:00Z","title":"First Entry","content":"Hello world content","tags":["work"],"priority":2},{"id":1,"date":"2020-02-01T00:00:00Z","title":"Second Entry","content":"body of second","tags":[],"priority":null},{"id":2,"date":"2026-08-09T00:00:00Z","title":"Third Entry","content":"","tags":["alpha","beta","","gamma"],"priority":5}]
```
- Field order per entry: `id`, `date`, `title`, `content`, `tags`, `priority`.
- `id`: integer, **starts at 0**, assigned as max-existing-id + 1 (verified: after deleting id 1 from {0,1,2}, a new entry got id 3; ids are NOT renumbered on delete — file kept `id:0` and `id:2`).
- `date`: RFC3339 UTC, always midnight: `"YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z"` (date-only precision; created entries use today's date by default). Importing `"2021-01-01T10:20:30+03:00"` is normalized to `"2021-01-01T07:20:30Z"`.
- `tags`: JSON array of strings; empty → `[]`.
- `priority`: unsigned int or JSON `null` when unset.
- `content`: string; empty → `""`.
- Empty backend (fresh home after `assign-priority` run): file contains exactly `[]` (2 bytes, no newline).
- File is rewritten immediately on every mutation (create/save/delete), not only on quit.

### Creating entries via TUI (`n` → "Create journal" popup)
- Fields (top→bottom): **Title**, **Date** (prefilled `DD-MM-YYYY`, e.g. `09-08-2026`; cursor starts at position 0; Backspace at pos 0 does nothing, forward-Delete `\x1b[3~` clears chars), **Priority**, **Tags** (label when focused: `Tags - A comma-separated list`).
- Footer: `Enter or <Ctrl-m>: confirm | Esc or <Ctrl-c>: Cancel | Tab: Change focused control | <Ctrl-Space> or <Ctrl-t>: Open tags`
- Date is validated live; error text replaces the field title, e.g. `Date : input contains invalid characters` (typing letters), `Date : input is out of range` (garbage digits), `Date : premature end of input` (partial). Enter with invalid date does NOT confirm.
- Priority field accepts digits (empty = null).
- Tags typed as `alpha, beta ,,gamma` → stored as `["alpha","beta","","gamma"]` (trimmed, empty segment kept as `""`).

payload.resultSummary:
Scope complete. Full notes written to `/tmp/tj/notes/backends-data.md`. Key findings: **JSON backend** (`$HOME/tui-journal/entries.json`): compact single-line array, no trailing newline. Entry field order `id,date,title,content,tags,priority`. ids start at **0**, assigned max+1, never renumbered on delete. Dates are `"YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z"` (UTC midnight). Empty priority → `null`, empty tags → `[]`, empty content → `""`. Tags typed as comma-separated list are trimmed but empty segments kept (`"alpha, beta ,,gamma"` → `["alpha","beta","","gamma"]`). File rewritten on every mutation. Create dialog validates the `DD-MM-YYYY` date live with chrono-style error strings in the field title. **state.json** (`$HOME/.local/state/tui-journal/state.json`): pretty-printed 2-space, no trailing newline; `{"sorter":{"criteria":["Date","Priority"],"order":"Descending"},"full_screen":false}`. Written **only on clean quit**; loaded at startup. Sort popup `o` (Space moves criteria between Applied/Available, `o` toggles order, Ctrl-d default) and `Ctrl-f` full screen both persist here. **SQLite backend** (`entries.db`): sqlx migrations table (3 migrations: `init entries`, `add tags`, `entries priorities`) + `entries(id INTEGER PK, title TEXT NOT NULL, date DATE, content TEXT, priority INTEGER DEFAULT NULL)` + `tags(entry_id, tag, PK(entry_id,tag), FK ON DELETE CASCADE)`. ids start at **1**. Date stored as TEXT `'...T00:00:00+00:00'` (not `Z`). Empty content = `''`, priority NULL. **assign-priority (ap)**: PRIORITY is u32 (clap range errors, exit 2). Requires a TTY — non-TTY gives `Error: No such device or address (os error 6)`, exit 1. On TTY: shows `Assigning Priority to Journals...` msgbox, updates **only null-priority entries**, writes the file immediately, then opens the full TUI (quit `q` → exit 0). No confirmation prompt. Fresh home creates `[]` entries.json / empty-schema db. Corrupt json → in-TUI `Error` msgbox `Error while parsing entries json data`, file untouched; corrupt db → `Error: error returned from database: (code: 26) file is not a database` + `Caused by:` block, exit 1. **import-journals (imj)**: transfer format (found via multi-select `v`→`a`→`>` export) is `{"version":100,"entries":[{date,title,content,tags,priority}]}` — pretty 2-space, no trailing newline, no ids, entry field order date/title/content/tags/priority. `version` is required **u16 but its value is ignored** (99/200/65535 all import). `priority` optional (defaults null); unknown keys (incl. `id`) ignored; all other fields required with exact serde error messages recorded in the notes. Merge = append with fresh ids, full duplication on re-import, dates normalized to UTC. Missing file → msgbox `Import file doesn't exist: path

`. Malformed → msgbox `Error while parsing import file.` + `Error: ` + `(O)k`, backend untouched. Export default path is **CWD-relative** `./tjournal_export.json`, written in storage order, overwrites silently, success `Info` msgbox `Journal(s) exported to file `. Tooling left behind: `/tmp/tj/bd/screen.py` (VT screen renderer), `/tmp/tj/bd/runpty.py` (pty runner with exit codes), plus all test homes/transfer files under `/tmp/tj/bd/`.

# Scope: tui-popups — popups & secondary screens of /workspace/executable (tui-journal 0.16.1)

All observations by running the binary under the PTY harness (`/tmp/tj/harness.py`), screens
rendered with `/tmp/tj/vtparse.py` (written by this agent; another agent later patched its SGR
handling). Sizes: 80x24 (default) and 120x40/120x30 where noted. Raw captures in `/tmp/tj/pop/*.raw`.

Fixture HOMEs: `/tmp/tj/popA` (5 entries, no content), `/tmp/tj/popB` (same + content),
`/tmp/tj/popEmpty` (no entries). Fixture entries (sqlite backend, `entries.db` table
`entries(id,title,date,content,priority)`; dates stored RFC3339 `2020-02-01T00:00:00+00:00`):

| id | title   | date (input dd-mm-yyyy) | priority | tags (typed)     | content      |
|----|---------|-------------------------|----------|------------------|--------------|
| 1  | Alpha   | 01-02-2020              | 2        | "work, urgent"   | apple        |
| 2  | Beta    | 15-06-2021              | (none)   | personal         | cherry date  |
| 3  | Gamma   | 10-10-2022              | 5        | work             | banana cherry|
| 4  | Delta   | 05-05-2023              | 1        | urgent           | apple banana |
| 5  | Epsilon | 20-12-2019              | 3        | (none)           | (empty)      |

Tags typed "work, urgent" display as "urgent | work" (sorted alphabetically, " | " separator).
Default list order: Date Descending (Delta, Gamma, Beta, Alpha, Epsilon). Default focus/cursor
is on the first entry; selected entry marked "> ", footer counter "1/5" bottom-right of list.

`n`, title, Tab, End (`\x1b[F`), 10x Backspace (clears prefilled today date; cursor starts at

## 2. Filter popup ('f')

Layout at 120x40 (titles exact; popup titled "Filter", square border ┌─┐):
- `╭Matching Logic╮` (ROUNDED border ╭╮╰╯) — interior centered text, default:
  `Journals must meet all criteria`; `<Ctrl-r>` toggles to `Journals must meet any of the criteria` (and back). Ctrl-r works regardless of focus.
- `┌Title─┐` text input (default focus on open)
- `┌Content─┐` text input
- `┌Priority─┐` text input (digits)
- `╭Tags─╮` (rounded border) multi-select list of ALL tags across journals, plus a synthetic last
  entry `NO_TAGS (Entries with no tags)`. Cursor line prefixed `>> `, other lines `   `;
  selected tags get `* ` after the prefix, e.g. `>> * urgent`. j/k or arrows move, `<Space>` toggles.

Footer (3 lines at 80x24, 2 at 120x40):
`Tab: Change focused control | Enter or <Ctrl-m>: Confirm | Esc or <Ctrl-c>: Cancel | <Ctrl-r>: Change Matching Logic | <Space>: Tags Toggle Selected`

Tab order: Title → Content → Priority → Tags → (Matching Logic?) → wraps. Verified: 0 Tabs=Title,
1=Content, 2=Priority, 3=Tags.

Behavior (all verified against fixtures):
- Title filter: case-SENSITIVE substring on title. `amm`→Gamma only; `AMM`→no matches.
- Content filter: substring on content. `cherry`→Gamma+Beta.
- Priority filter: exact equality. `2`→Alpha only.
- Tags: entries must have selected tag(s); `urgent`→Delta+Alpha; `NO_TAGS`→Epsilon only.
- Matching logic ALL (default) = criteria ANDed; ANY = ORed (title `zzz` + tag urgent with ANY →
  Delta+Alpha).
- Invalid priority (non-numeric, e.g. `abc`): typing shows validation in the box title:
  `Priority : Priority must be a positive number`; Enter does NOT close the popup (confirm blocked).
- Enter applies and closes. Applied filter changes the journals-list block title to
  `Journals - Filtered` and the footer item `Open filter: 'f'` becomes `Reset filter: 'x'`.
- Reopening 'f' shows the previously applied values (Title prefilled `amm` etc.) — filter persists
  for the session (NOT written to state.json; state.json only has sorter+full_screen).
- Esc / Ctrl-c cancels: no changes applied.
- 'x' on main screen resets filter (list title back to `Journals`); with no active filter 'x' is a no-op.
- Empty result: list shows same placeholder as empty journal list
  (`Use 'n' to create new` / `       entry` at rows 3-4), no `n/N` counter.
- Quirk: after 'x' reset the Content pane briefly shows the previously selected entry's content
  while the cursor is back on the first entry (stale content pane).
- Quirk at 80x24: Title/Content/Priority boxes render as 2 rows (no interior), typed text not echoed;
  Matching Logic interior text also hidden. Input still works.
- Empty journal list: 'f' opens normally; Tags box shows centered `No journals with tags provided`.

### Ctrl-t (cycle tag filter, main screen, no popup)
Cycles the tag filter through each tag alphabetically then NO_TAGS, e.g. with fixture tags:
press 1 → personal (Beta only), 2 → urgent (Delta, Alpha), 3 → work, 4 → NO_TAGS (Epsilon only),
5 → wraps to personal again. There is NO "unfiltered" step in the cycle — use 'x' to clear.
List title shows `Journals - Filtered` while active.

---

## 3. Sort popup ('o')

Popup titled "Sort" (square border). Widgets:
- `┌Sort Order─┐` box, centered content `Descending` (default) — pressing `o` toggles to
  `Ascending`. Initial focus.
- `╭Available Criteria─╮` (rounded) — initially contains `Title` (cursor `>> Title`).
- `╭Applied Criteria─╮` (rounded) — initially `>> Date`, `   Priority` (default sort = Date then
  Priority, Descending).
- When the last applied criterion is removed, the Applied box title changes to
  `Applied criteria can't be empty` and Enter will not confirm.

Footer (focus = Sort Order box):
`Tab: Change focused control | Enter or <Ctrl-m>: Confirm | Esc or <Ctrl-c>: Cancel |<o>: Change Sort Order | <Space>: Move criteria to other list |<j/k> or <up/down> cycle between criteria | <Ctrl-d> Load default`
Footer when focus = Applied Criteria list — extra segment appears:
`... |<j/k> or <up/down> cycle between criteria | <Ctrl-j/k> or <Ctrl-Up/Down> Move criteria up/down | <Ctrl-d> Load default`

Tab order: Sort Order → Applied Criteria → Available Criteria → wrap.
- `<Space>` moves the cursor's criterion to the other list (into Available appended at end; into
  Applied appended at end). Verified: Tab,Space moves Date out (Available: Title, Date; Applied:
  Priority); Tab,Tab,Space moves Title into Applied (Date, Priority, Title).
- `<Ctrl-j>` in Applied moves criterion down (Date moved below Priority).
- `<Ctrl-d>` loads default (Date, Priority / Descending) into the popup.
- Enter confirms & applies; Esc cancels (list order unchanged).
- Applied sort Title/Ascending produced list: Alpha, Beta, Delta, Epsilon, Gamma; the cursor stays
  on the previously selected entry (Delta, counter 3/5).
- state.json (`$HOME/.local/state/tui-journal/state.json`) is written on clean quit ('q') and
  read at startup; after the above sort + 'q' it contained exactly:
  ```json
  {
    "sorter": {
      "criteria": [
        "Title"
      ],
      "order": "Ascending"
    },
    "full_screen": false
  }
  ```
  Default (fresh home) is criteria ["Date","Priority"], order "Descending". Reopening 'o' shows
  the persisted criteria/order. (state.json is NOT written if the process is killed; only on 'q'.)
- Works with an empty journal list (popup fully usable).

---

## 4. Fuzzy find popup ('a' or Shift-F)

Rounded-border popup titled "Fuzzy Find", containing:
- `┌Search Query─┐` input (starts empty)
- `┌Entries: N─┐` list box — N = match count; **0 when the query is empty**. Matching entries
  shown with `>> ` cursor prefix / `   ` others.
- Footer: `Esc, Enter, <Ctrl-m>, <Ctrl-c>: Close | Up, Down, <Ctrl-n>, <Ctrl-p>: cycle through filtered list`

Behavior:
- Real fuzzy subsequence match on TITLES, CASE-SENSITIVE: query `a` → Alpha, Delta, Gamma, Beta
  (Epsilon has no 'a'); query `gm` → Gamma (subsequence, not substring); query `A` → Alpha only.
- Results are ordered by fuzzy score, NOT list order: `a` gave Alpha, Delta, Gamma, Beta.
- Typing live-updates the main list: cursor jumps to the top match (query `a` → `> Alpha`, 4/5,
  Content pane shows its content).
- Up/Down/Ctrl-n/Ctrl-p move the `>>` cursor in the match list and the main-list selection follows
  live. Closing (Enter AND Esc alike) keeps the last highlighted entry selected — Esc does NOT
  revert to the pre-popup selection.
- Quirk: with rapid repeated Down presses the cycle order looked inconsistent under the harness
  (Down x1 → Delta; Down x2 sometimes → Beta skipping Gamma, once → Delta again; Down x3 → Delta,
  x4 → Gamma). Single presses are reliable; possibly the list re-sorts around the selection or
  key events race with redraws. Record as "cycling order may be unstable with fast input".
- Empty journal list: popup opens, `Entries: 0`.
- Enter closes and the entry stays selected (then Enter again opens its editor, etc.).

---

## 5. Multi-select mode ('v')

- Entered with 'v' from the journals list. List block title becomes `Journals - Multi-Selec`
  (truncated at 80 cols; full text presumably "Journals - Multi-Select"). Footer (1 row):
  `Leave journals multi selection mode: 'q','v','Esc','<Ctrl-c>' | Show help: '?'`
- Leave with q / v / Esc / Ctrl-c (mode title and footer revert).
- Toggle current entry: Space / Enter / Ctrl-m. Selected entries are prefixed `* ` after the
  list marker, e.g. `> * Delta` (cursor+selected) and `  * Gamma` (selected, not cursor).
- `a` select all (all get `* `), `x` clear selection, `i` invert (verified: Delta selected → invert
  → Delta unselected, other 4 selected).
- `d` with a non-empty selection opens the bulk delete confirmation (see §6), text:
  `Do you want to delete the selected 5 entries` (count interpolated). 'd' with EMPTY selection:
  nothing happens.
- After bulk delete the mode STAYS active; with no entries left the list shows
  `No entries to select` (row 3).
- Empty journal list: 'v' still enters the mode; list shows `No entries to select`.
- No bulk priority/tag operations exist (not in help; only delete is wired).

---

## 6. Delete confirmation msgbox ('d', Delete, Ctrl-d)

All three keys (`d`, `\x1b[3~`, `\x04`) behave identically. Box: plain square border, NO title,
44 cols wide × 8 rows, centered (80x24: rows 9-16, cols 19-62). Byte-exact (from
`/tmp/tj/pop/delete_prompt.raw`):
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                          │
│     Do you want to remove the current    │
│                 journal?                 │
│                                          │
│               (Y)es , (N)o               │
│                                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
Single delete text: `Do you want to remove the current journal?` (centered, wrapped).
Bulk delete text: `Do you want to delete the selected 5 entries` (count varies).
Buttons line: `(Y)es , (N)o` (note spacing: `(Y)es , (N)o`).

Keys: `y` = yes (delete), `n` = no (cancel), Esc = cancel, **Enter = YES (default) — confirmed:
Enter deleted the entry**. After delete the cursor moves to the next entry (Delta deleted →
Gamma selected, counter 1/4).
Empty journal list: 'd' is a no-op (no popup).

---

## 7. Export popup ('>')

Popup titled "Export journal content" (square border). Contents:
- Line: `Journal: Delta` (title of current entry)
- `┌Path─┐` input prefilled with `<cwd>/<Title>.txt` — observed `/tmp/tj/Delta.txt` when the
  process cwd was /tmp/tj. Cursor starts at position 0 (End key needed to edit the tail).
- Footer: `Enter: confirm | Esc or <Ctrl-c>: Cancel`

Behavior:
- Enter exports the RAW content bytes only (file `/tmp/tj/Delta.txt` = `b'apple banana'`, no
  trailing newline, no metadata) and shows an Info msgbox (title "Info"):
  ```
  ┌Info──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                          │
  │     Journal content exported to file     │
  │             /tmp/tj/Delta.txt            │
  │                                          │
  │                   (O)k                   │
  │                                          │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ```
  (path line = the entered path). Dismiss with 'o' or Enter (both verified).
- Export CREATES missing parent directories (`/no/such/dir/x.txt` succeeded and was created).
- A truly unwritable path (`/proc/x.txt`) shows an Error msgbox (title "Error"):
  `Error while exporting journal(s). Err: No such file or directory (os error 2)` with `(O)k`.
- Empty path + Enter: blocked with validation in the Path box title: `Path : Path can't be empty`.
- Esc cancels. Empty journal list: '>' is a no-op (no popup).

---

## 8. Msgbox styling summary (default theme)

- All msgboxes: centered, 44 wide, plain `┌─┐` square borders; question boxes untitled,
  Info/Error boxes titled `Info` / `Error` in the top border. Text centered, word-wrapped.
- Buttons: `(Y)es , (N)o` for questions (y/n/Esc/Enter keys; Enter=Yes), `(O)k` for Info/Error
  (dismiss: 'o' or Enter).
- No colors in the default theme — the only SGR codes seen in all captures are
  `\x1b[1m` (bold), `\x1b[22m`, `\x1b[;m`, `\x1b[m`, `\x1b[0m`, `\x1b[2m` (dim). Bold is used for
  the main-pane border/title lines. Cursor hidden (`\x1b[?25l`) after every frame.
- (Custom `themes.toml` exists for msgbox styling per THEMES.md `[msgbox]` group — not explored
  here; theme scope belongs to another agent.)

## 9. Esc / cancel behavior summary

| Context | Esc effect |
|---|---|
| Filter popup | cancels, no filter change |
| Sort popup | cancels, sort unchanged |
| Fuzzy find | closes, KEEPS the live-highlighted entry selected |
| Create/export popups | cancels, nothing created/exported |
| Delete prompt | cancels (same as 'n') |
| Info/Error msgbox | (not tested; 'o'/Enter work) |
| Help popup | closes |
| Multi-select mode | leaves mode |
| Ctrl-c works as cancel in all popups too (per footers) |

## 10. Validation-message pattern

Input-box validation messages are appended to the box TITLE with `" : "` separator:
`Title : Title can't be empty`, `Path : Path can't be empty`,
`Priority : Priority must be a positive number`, and sort popup's
`Applied criteria can't be empty` (replaces the whole title). Also seen in create popup date
field: `Date : trailing input` when the date text is malformed (typing at cursor pos 0 produced
`01-02-202009-08-2026`).

## 11. Raw captures saved (for byte-level reference, /tmp/tj/pop/)

- `filter_open.raw` / `filter_themed.raw` — filter popup at 80x24
- `delete_prompt.raw` — delete confirmation, byte-exact box quoted in §6
- `help_popup.raw` (in /tmp/tj/bd/, from another agent) — help popup frame 1
- plus various `*.raw` for create/date edit flows.
Render any with: `python3 /tmp/tj/vtparse.py <file> [--rows N --cols M] [--runs|--attrs]`
